title: Define management and describe the management process and the functions of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling
Explain why management is important to an organisation
Compare the schools of management thought: classical, neoclassical or behavioural, quantitative, systems, contingency and contemporary (total quality management and the learning organisation)
Describe the challenges and opportunities facing management: business models, information explosion, managing change, globalisation and environmental sustainability
Explain strategic management: strategy and plan, types of strategy, vision and mission, the elements and phases of strategic management and its benefits
Explain business environment analysis and why a manager must understand the external environment
Explain what planning is, the steps in the planning process and why planning is important
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of planning
Explain management by objectives: the MBO process, SMART goals, limitations and advantages

Describe the components of a plan, including environmental analysis (PESTLE and SWOT), internal analysis tools, fixation of objectives, planning premises, evaluation of alternatives and finalisation of the plan
Explain contingency planning and what a contingency plan covers
Explain forecasting (long, medium and short term) and decision making, including group decisions, conditions of decision making and principles of decision making
